profile.audience: 22-year-olds who just started their first job

research_material:
nobody taught me how to budget
I'm always broke by the 15th and I don't know why

pain_points: Money disappears before mid-month with no visibility into where
No system or framework for tracking spending
Feeling helpless and confused about financial management

hooks.text: Your bank statement is bleeding $200/month and you have no idea.
I found where your paycheck disappears every single month.
That promotion money? Gone. Here's the audit.
You're not bad with money. You're just subscribed to 12 things.
Real bank statement audit: watching someone's first job money vanish.
Your parents were right about one thing: you're wasteful.
Broke after payday? Let me show you exactly why.
Most 22-year-olds leak $250+ monthly. You're probably one of them.
Line-by-line bank statement audit reveals the brutal truth.
You think you're saving. Your subscriptions disagree.

winner.text: Your bank statement is bleeding $200/month and you have no idea.
winner.reasoning: This hits the exact pain point of someone who just got their first paycheck and doesn't yet understand cash leakage. The word 'bleeding' is visceral and urgent, making it immediately relatable—they feel the money loss but can't articulate it. The 'no idea' part triggers the curiosity gap while the blunt tone matches the brand voice perfectly for Gen Z.

runner_up.text: Broke after payday? Let me show you exactly why.
runner_up.reasoning: This works because it directly addresses the bewildering Gen Z experience of mysteriously being broke despite earning income. It's relatable, action-oriented, and promises a solution, making it safer while still maintaining edge.

script.script: [HOOK - 0-3 sec] [ON-SCREEN TEXT: Your bank statement is bleeding $200/month] Your bank statement is bleeding $200/month and you have no idea. [PAUSE] [CUT] [PROBLEM - 3-8 sec] That's subscriptions you forgot about. Apps you opened once. Gym memberships that haunt you. Small charges that feel invisible until you do the math. [ON-SCREEN TEXT: $15 × 12 = $180/year PER subscription] [CUT] [VALUE - 8-15 sec] Here's what actually works: [ON-SCREEN TEXT: AUDIT YOUR APPS] Go through your bank app right now. Screenshot every charge under $20. [ON-SCREEN TEXT: UNSUBSCRIBE] Cancel anything you haven't used in 30 days. Yes, actually cancel it. Don't just say you will. [ON-SCREEN TEXT: SET A RULE] New subscriptions only if you cancel an old one. One in, one out. That's it. [PAUSE] [ON-SCREEN TEXT: $200/month = $2,400/year] [CUT] [CTA - 15-17 sec] Save this before payday. Actually do it.
script.viewer_takeaway: Identify and eliminate forgotten subscriptions to reclaim $200+ monthly through a simple three-step audit system.

cover_options: Split screen: left side shows a red-bleeding bank statement graphic, right side shows shocked person staring at phone. Bold white text overlay: '$200/month GONE' with a skull emoji
Close-up of a hand swiping through phone banking app, with red X marks appearing over subscription logos (Netflix, Spotify, Gym, etc.). Text: 'Your money is disappearing' in harsh sans-serif font

frame_plan.visual_direction: Animated bank statement on black background with red liquid/blood effect dripping down. Zoom in on a '$200' figure highlighted in red. Quick cut to confused person's face.
Rapid montage of app icons (Netflix, Spotify, DoorDash, Peloton, etc.) with shake effect. Each icon gets a red 'X' or cancellation symbol overlaid.
Math animation: $15 icon bounces 12 times across screen, then transforms into '$180' in bold red text. Show a stack of money shrinking away.

frame_plan.on_screen_text: AUDIT YOUR APPS – screenshot every charge under $20
frame_plan.visual_direction: Hand holding phone, swiping through banking app. Screenshot camera click sound effect. Bank statement highlighted with yellow markers on small charges.

frame_plan.on_screen_text: UNSUBSCRIBE – cancel if unused in 30 days
frame_plan.visual_direction: Finger tapping 'Cancel Subscription' button with heavy emphasis. Red 'CANCELLED' stamp appears on screen. Satisfying click/delete sound effect.

frame_plan.on_screen_text: SET A RULE – one in, one out
frame_plan.visual_direction: Simple scale graphic: subscription icon removed from left side, new subscription added to right side, scale balances. Clean, minimalist design.
Large '$2,400' appears with money animation (bills/coins floating away). Dramatic beat. Cut to black.

frame_plan.on_screen_text: Save this. Do it before payday.
frame_plan.visual_direction: Text appears in aggressive sans-serif against black background. Quick flash of save/bookmark icon. Final frame: person nodding with determined expression.

assets_needed: Bank statement graphic template (editable for red bleeding effect)
App icon set (Netflix, Spotify, DoorDash, Peloton, Gym, etc.)
Phone screen recordings (banking app, subscription cancellation flow)
Red X and cancellation stamp graphics
Shocked/determined person B-roll (close-ups of face reactions)
Hand animations (scrolling, tapping, swiping on phone)
Sound effects: click, cash register, stamp sound, satisfying 'delete' chime
Font: Bold sans-serif (system font acceptable – aim for aggressive/blunt feel)
Color palette: Black background, white/red text, yellow highlights

justifications.clarity: Hook lands in 1 second with a specific, quantified problem ($200/month) that requires no context.
justifications.retention: Problem-to-solution structure with visible progress (audit → unsubscribe → rule) keeps momentum, though middle lacks emotional spike.
justifications.save_potential: $2,400/year visualization plus three actionable steps make this immediately bookmark-worthy for the target demo.
justifications.shareability: Relatable frustration and shocking annual math ($2,400) drive shares, but lacks the surprise/humor twist that makes Gen Z tag friends.
justifications.audience_fit: First-job earners bleed subscriptions; forgotten charges and $15/month pain points are core Gen Z financial anxiety.
justifications.cta_strength: Direct, low-friction ask ('Save this before payday') + urgency tie (payday reference) works for audience that responds to deadline language.

weaknesses.issue: No emotional peak in the middle—transitions from problem shock to solution steps without a 'gut punch' moment that drives shares.
weaknesses.fix: Add a 6-second interpolation between PROBLEM detail and VALUE step 1: 'If you do nothing, that's a car payment. A trip. Your first apartment deposit.' Paired with rapid cuts of aspirational imagery (car keys, beach, apartment keys) to reframe the money loss as opportunity cost, not just a number.

weaknesses.issue: Shareability gap: post solves the problem but doesn't give viewers a reason to tag a friend or send it to their group chat.
weaknesses.fix: Rewrite CTA to 'Save this AND send it to the friend who has 7 subscriptions they forgot about.' Then add a 1-second frame of someone laughing/nodding with text overlay 'that's probably you.' Makes it social-first.

weaknesses.issue: The 'one in, one out' rule is clever but visually underexplained—scale graphic alone won't land the behavior shift needed for actual adoption.
weaknesses.fix: Expand VALUE step 3 from 3 seconds to 4 seconds with a concrete example: 'Want HBO Max? Cancel DoorDash. Want Peloton? Kill the gym app. Every subscription must earn its spot.' Pair with side-by-side before/after of phone home screens (cluttered vs. clean) to make the constraint feel like a win, not a restriction.

captions: Your subscriptions are stealing $2,400/year and you don't even know their names. Here's how to get it back before payday hits. Save this. 🔴
Bleeding $200/month to apps you forgot existed? Audit, cancel, set a rule. That's $2,400 back in your pocket. Save + send this to someone who needs to hear it.
growth.final_call_reason: High clarity and audience fit, but shareability score dips because the post solves a problem without giving it social velocity—add emotional reframe (opportunity cost) and friend-tagging mechanic to unlock natural distribution on TikTok.
